items.title: Exhumation of Mir Raza Ali's body postponed after family objects to abrupt reconstitution of medico-legal board
items.description: KARACHI: The exhumation of 25-year-old businessman and Institute of Business Administration graduate Mir Raza Ali’s body was postponed on Friday after his family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of the medico-legal board. Ali’s body was found in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28. While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, investigators probing the incident continue to build their case around the possibility that he died by suicide. His family was present at the cemetery adjacent to Tariq Road’s Rehmania Masjid for the exhumation on Friday. But, the exhumation was deferred, with the counsel for Ali’s family, Jibran Nasir, telling the media that they had informed the investigating officer that the family had rejected the reconstituted board and would not accept an exhumation by it “under any circumstances”. Standing alongside Ali’s father, Mir Hussain Ali Khan, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts and held the police, health ministry and the Sindh government responsible for the delay. The family could not allow the examination to be performed by members whose “qualifications and intentions were under question”, he added. He recalled that the previous night, Hyderabad health director general dismissed the original board and reconstituted it, adding four names from Hyderabad. Nasir claimed that following outcry over the reconstituted board, the DG health then issued a backdated notification at around 10am on Friday. “He says more members may be added [to the board], but the four chosen by him should also remain a part of it,” Nasir alleged. He added that they still had not been informed why the original board was reconstituted. Moreover, he continued, now there was another notification that authorised the Hyderabad health director general to form the medico-legal board, a power that previously rested with the Sindh health secretary. The authorities “needed to be given a lesson on law” as under the Sindh Medicolegal Act 2023, only a police surgeon had the complete authority in matters of exhumation, he said, adding that the act was a special law that prevailed over general laws. The lawyer said they would not be making any demands to the police. Ali’s father was now directly raising questions to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, he said. “We will also not turn to the Sindh inspector general of police (IG). What do you ask an IG who claims that the investigation has been completed even before the exhumation and medical examination?” He reasserted that they only trusted the original eight-member board, adding, “Sindh government, they were hired by you. And if they are not competent enough, then how were they appointed in the first place?” Nasir alleged that police were presenting the CCTV evidence “selectively” and demanded that all facts of the case be brought to light. He said CCTV footage shared showed a motorcycle and a trash picker passing by the body. But then, why did it not show the moment when Ali walked up to the place where his body was found, if he died by suicide, Nasir questioned. “Where did that footage go?” He added, “Why is it that people at the nearby guesthouse panicked and ran to a nearby property when Ali’s father inquired about him? […] And why were they not tracked?” Nasir further accused police of not letting Ali’s father see the complete CCTV footage. Concluding his talk, he said, “If not today, then maybe we will get the exhumation done tomorrow. We will try our best that the originally nominated doctors perform the examination, and I am sure the facts that they are going to such great lengths to bury will surface.” Speaking to reporters earlier in the day, the family’s counsel said that the Sindh Medicolegal Act 2023 required that if a magistrate issues an order for exhumation, the authority to form a board rested with the division’s police surgeon. “I believe I am standing in Karachi division where the police surgeon is Dr Summaiya Syed […] who would constitute the board and add forensic experts from the nearest possible public sector university,” Nasir said, questioning whether Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences was closer to Karachi than Dow Medical College or the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC). Nasir alleged that the “illegal and dubious” board had no authority to examine the body. “We cannot allow them to disrespect the deceased and destroy evidence.” He also asked how a fresh notification was issued when the previous one had not yet been withdrawn, alleging that a third party and a “stranger” to the proceedings had intervened. “We will not accept any Plan C either,” he said, referring to the suggestion to merge the two boards. Earlier, he had also alleged on X that the Sindh government had “maliciously” changed the members of the board without any explanation. “The family expresses no consent for this new board and will not allow it to exhumate the body tomorrow morning and corrupt whatever evidence remains and it will be formally communicated to authorities,” he said, adding that the fresh notification would be challenged at the appropriate forum. ‘Malicious attempt to interfere with judicial proceedings’ Nasir also submitted a letter to the police surgeon on Friday, wherein he formally informed her of the family’s non-consent and stated that the reconstituted board was in “complete violation and negation” of the court’s order and had no legal basis. He held that it carried no binding value and was nothing “but a malicious attempt to interfere with judicial proceedings initiated by the court” and any directive in support of the board shall be viewed as a “further malicious attempt to provide cover to an illegal act and sabotage fair and transparent investigation”. Nasir said the family had not consented to the exhumation by the reconstituted board and warned that any attempt to proceed with the exhumation under the reconstituted medical board will be a violation of the dignity of the deceased, will put evidence at risk and will be a “blatant” contempt of court. He said the police surgeon that she remained “duty bound” to conduct the exhumation with the original medical board and further held that the action had “fortified the apprehension of our clients that instead of investigating the truth every effort is being made to suppress the truth and manipulate evidence and facts to arrive at a pre-determined outcome by the senior officers of police and the same is being done at behest of influentials who are being protected in the investigation into the death of Mir Raza Ali Khan”. He concluded that in case of any further proceedings through the “illegally constituted” board, the family had the right to approach the appropriate court and seek prosecution of the officers attempting to “jeopardise” the investigation. Reconstitution of board On Thursday, a Karachi court allowed the exhumation of Ali’s body on an application filed by Ali’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medico-legal board for the exhumation of Ali’s body “at the earliest possible date and time”. The court ruling came after a controversy emerged between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding the post-mortem examination. The Sindh health department then constituted the eight-member board, with Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed as the convener. Prof Dr Naseem Ahmed of Dow University of Health Sciences (DUHS), Dr Farah Waseem of Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Amir Hassan Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre and Dr Mohammed Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon office, were the other members of the board. However, a new order has been issued by the Sindh health directorate general. The notification, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said that the board had been reconstituted to conduct the exhumation and medico-legal examination of the deceased. While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan. Controversy over autopsy Raza, an IBA graduate and the owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. Initially, on the complaint lodged by his father, a case was registered at the Ferozabad police station under Section 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine a person) of the Pakistan Penal Code. Police maintain that the investigation has revealed that Ali had been facing financial difficulties and had asked his friends for money the night he died. According to police, he had left his home in PECHS Block-2 and hired a taxi through an app. The taxi driver dropped him a short distance from the spot where his body was found, police said. The case took a new turn when Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel on Tuesday that the postmortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. She said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another. While it was scientifically possible for a bullet to enter through the back and exit from the front, she stressed that her assessment was based only on the postmortem report and photographs, as she had not examined the body herself. The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case. Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation. The statement, however, said that exhumation of the dead body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission.

items.title: Gourma : Le Cadre régional de dialogue évalue à mi-parcours l’exécution des Plans d’action régionaux de développement
items.description: BURKINA-GOULMOU-SIRBA-TAPOA-DÉVELOPPEMENT-CRD Gourma : Le Cadre régional de dialogue évalue à mi-parcours l'exécution des Plans d'action régionaux de développement Fada N'Gourma, 6 août 2026 (AIB)-Le Gouverneur de la région du Goulmou, Ram Joseph Kafando, a présidé, le jeudi 06 août 2026 à Fada N'Gourma, la troisième session ordinaire du Cadre régional de dialogue (CRD), consacrée à la revue à mi-parcours 2026 des Plans d'actions régionaux de développement (PARD) du Goulmou, de la Sirba et de la Tapoa. La cérémonie a connu la présence des autorités administratives, militaires et paramilitaires, des partenaires techniques et financiers, des partenaires humanitaires et des représentants de la société civile. Les membres du CRD ont examiné les rapports de performance à mi-parcours des trois régions. Les échanges ont permis d'apprécier les progrès enregistrés dans plusieurs secteurs prioritaires, notamment le renforcement des capacités opérationnelles en matière de sécurité, la promotion de la cohésion sociale et de la protection sociale, le développement des infrastructures sanitaires et éducatives, l'appui aux producteurs agricoles, la promotion de l’emploi ainsi que le renforcement de la gouvernance locale. Selon le Gouverneur de la région du Goulmou, Ram Joseph Kafando, au 30 juin 2026, sur 417 actions programmées dans l'ensemble des 03 régions, 120 ont été entièrement réalisées et 81 sont en cours d'exécution, soit un taux d'exécution physique de 39 %. Sur le plan financier, les dépenses réalisées s'élèvent à 11,572 milliards de FCFA sur une prévision de 25,5 milliards de FCFA, correspondant à un taux d'exécution financière de 46 %. Le premier responsable de la région a salué l'engagement des services techniques, des collectivités territoriales, des projets et programmes, des organisations de la société civile ainsi que des communautés locales qui, malgré un contexte difficile, poursuivent la mise en œuvre des PARD. Il a toutefois invité l'ensemble des acteurs à redoubler d'efforts au cours du second semestre, notamment en matière de mobilisation des ressources, de célérité dans les procédures de passation des marchés, de renforcement des capacités opérationnelles des forces de sécurité et d'amélioration de la collaboration avec les forces combattantes, afin d'atteindre les objectifs fixés en fin d'année. Agence d’information du Burkina KAC/HB/OO

items.title: Atta Akyea says NPP’s protest seeks to highlight threats to Ghana’s democracy
items.description: Former Member of Parliament for Abuakwa South, Samuel Atta Akyea, says the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration was aimed at drawing attention to what he described as growing concerns over Ghana’s democratic principles under the administration of President John Dramani Mahama. Speaking to journalists after taking part in the protest on Thursday, August 6, Mr Atta Akyea said the demonstration was intended to remind citizens and political leaders that democracy must be protected regardless of which party is in power. He argued that Ghanaians have a responsibility to speak out whenever they believe democratic values, including freedom of expression and respect for divergent views, are being threatened. The former legislator maintained that freedom of expression is a key pillar of democracy and expressed concern over what he described as attempts to intimidate individuals for expressing opinions contrary to those of the government. “The main purpose of this demonstration is to bring to the fore that democracy is under attack and if our president, who is very experienced in our politics, should turn democracy upside down, then we should stand up to it and correct it. So this is essentially what we are saying. It is very important that we practice democracy in decency. “If somebody expresses a contrary opinion on television or even social media and then they go and fetch him, then we are coming back to square one,” he said. Mr Atta Akyea was speaking after participating in the NPP’s “Democracy Under Attack” protest, which brought together party executives, Members of Parliament, supporters and sympathisers who marched through parts of Accra to express concerns over what they described as threats to democratic governance, the rule of law and civil liberties.

items.title: Trump signs orders to limit US birthright citizenship, despite Supreme Court ruling
items.description: US President Donald Trump signed two executive orders on Thursday in a new but narrower attempt to curtail birthright citizenship, once again challenging a provision of the US Constitution even though the Supreme Court rejected his previous effort. Limiting birthright citizenship has been one of the top priorities in the Republican president’s crackdown on immigration, with the White House taking particular aim at what it calls “birth tourism,” in which pregnant foreigners travel to the US to give birth. After his June 30 setback in the Supreme Court, Trump called on Congress to act, but on Thursday he opted for executive orders, which set policy but do not carry the same weight as laws passed by Congress. The Supreme Court had struck down as unconstitutional Trump’s earlier executive order , which targeted a wide swath of immigrants in the country illegally or temporarily. The administration argues the new directive falls outside the purview of the Supreme Court ruling, as it seeks to reinterpret the narrow, historical exceptions to citizenship at birth and expand who is ineligible. “That practice of birth tourism is, as of the signing of this order, hereby banned,” White House aide Stephen Miller said at the Thursday signing ceremony in the Oval Office. The Centre for Immigration Studies, which supports lower levels of immigration, estimated in an analysis in 2020 that between 20,000 and 25,000 mothers came to the US for birth tourism in a year-long period between 2016 and 2017. There were 3.6 million births in the US in 2025. The executive orders also limit the rights of children born to foreign government employees in the US and children of people who are classified as alien enemies. The orders could also affect people born in US territories, should Congress enact a proposed law to end automatic citizenship there. Trump’s new orders are likely to face legal challenge. Legal experts said it was unclear what effect the executive orders might have given the Supreme Court ruling, while immigrant advocates called it an attempt to evade the high court’s decision. The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) predicted it was doomed to fail in court. “Just five weeks ago, the Supreme Court made clear that birthright citizenship is not subject to a president’s whims; it is a constitutional guarantee that has stood for more than 150 years. Today’s executive orders are nothing more than an attempt to get around that ruling,” said Deborah Fleischaker, a former Biden administration official who is now with UnidosUS, a Hispanic civil rights and advocacy organisation. Zain Lakhani of the Women’s Refugee Commission said the executive orders could trample the rights of pregnant women seeking lawful entry “in one of the most vulnerable moments of their lives”, and called on the government to establish guidelines honouring the Supreme Court ruling. ‘A very unfortunate decision’ Trump, speaking in the Oval Office on Thursday, called the Supreme Court’s 6-3 ruling on June 30 a “very unfortunate decision”, decrying that “people are building businesses around” birth tourism. “That’s not the way it’s supposed to work. It’s a disgrace. They’re buying their way in, and we’re not going to let it happen,” he said. Trump’s prior executive order, issued on his first day in office in 2025 as part of a suite of policies to crack down on immigration, directed US agencies not to recognise the citizenship of children born in the United States if neither parent is an American citizen or legal permanent resident, also called a “green card” holder — barring babies of immigrants in the US illegally or temporarily. The 14th Amendment has long been interpreted as guaranteeing citizenship for babies born in the US with only narrow exceptions such as the children of foreign diplomats or members of an enemy occupying force. “This was done for a different reason. This was done right after the Civil War. This was for the babies of slaves, and what’s happening now?” Trump said. There are no official figures tallying the number of foreigners who come to the US for the explicit purpose of giving birth and obtaining citizenship for their children, or the cost to taxpayers. In any case, Chief Justice John Roberts wrote in the Supreme Court ruling that the authors of the 14th Amendment extended that promise to every free-born person in the land. “Citizenship, then and now, was the right to have rights — to freely participate in our political community. We keep that promise today,” Roberts wrote. The 14th Amendment provision known as the Citizenship Clause states: “All persons born or naturalised in the United States, and subject to the jurisdiction thereof, are citizens of the United States and of the state wherein they reside.”

items.title: Léraba/Montée des couleurs : le Haut-commissaire appelle chacun à s’interroger sur son rôle dans la construction de la Nation
items.description: BURKINA-LERABA-MONTEE-DES-COULEURS-PATRIOTISME Léraba/Montée des couleurs : le Haut-commissaire appelle chacun à s’interroger sur son rôle dans la construction de la Nation Sindou, 6 août 2026 (AIB)-Le Haut-commissaire de la province de la Léraba, Yacouba Sawadogo, a présidé le jeudi 06 août 2026, la cérémonie mensuelle de montée tournante des couleurs nationales à la Direction provinciale de la Police nationale de la Léraba. Il a relayé le message du Président du Faso et a invité chaque citoyen à une profonde introspection sur sa contribution au devenir de la Nation. A 7 h 30 mn, le drapeau national a été hissé au sommet du mât au son du Ditanyè, entonné en chœur par les autorités administratives, les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), les corps constitués et les populations mobilisées dans l'enceinte de la Direction provinciale de la Police nationale à Sindou, chef-lieu de la province de la Léraba. Instituée en 2022 dans la Léraba, la montée collective et tournante des couleurs nationales vise à renforcer le civisme, l'amour de la patrie et le respect des symboles de l'Etat. Organisée chaque premier jeudi du mois, cette cérémonie connaît en 2026 une innovation. Désormais, elle se déroulera à tour de rôle, tous les deux mois, dans l'un des huit départements de la province, suivant l'ordre alphabétique, afin d'étendre cette dynamique patriotique à l'ensemble du territoire provincial. Le Haut-commissaire de la province de la Léraba, Yacouba Sawadogo a présenté les grandes lignes du message du Président du Faso relatif à la commémoration de la Révolution démocratique et populaire du 4 août 1984 ainsi qu'au 66e anniversaire de l'indépendance du Burkina Faso. Selon lui, ce message invite les Burkinabè à réfléchir sur leur responsabilité individuelle et collective dans la construction d'une Nation souveraine. « En vous relayant le contenu de ce message fort du chef de l'État, je voudrais inviter chacun de nous à une profonde introspection sur notre rôle respectif dans le devenir de notre Nation », a déclaré le Haut-commissaire. Le directeur provincial de la Police nationale de la Léraba, le commissaire principal Konlaré Sadock Hien, a présenté les missions de son service avant de rappeler les attitudes civiques à observer à l'égard du drapeau national et des autres symboles de l'État. Le Président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de la commune de Kankalaba, Blaise Arnaud Zomono, a reçu le flambeau symbolique. Il s'est engagé, avec ses collaborateurs, à réussir l'organisation de la prochaine cérémonie de montée des couleurs nationales, prévue le jeudi 3 septembre 2026 à Kankalaba. Agence d’information du Burkina MK/HB/OO

items.title: Schedule for 3rd phase of AJK polls revised over law and order concerns
items.description: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Election Commission on Friday revised the schedule for the third phase of elections in the region, saying polling would only be held in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts on August 10 amid concerns over the law and order situation. Elections are being held across AJK in three phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities. Polls in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively. The third phase in Poonch division was set for August 10. Poonch Division comprises 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti district. However, the Election Commission said in a press release on Friday that the electoral process will go ahead as planned on August 10 in only the division’s Bagh and Haveli districts. In its press release, the AJK Election Commission said polling will be held in the three constituencies of Bagh and one of Haveli on August 10 as per the previous schedule. However, the electoral process in the constituencies of Poonch district and Sudhnoti’s Pallandri will not be held on August 10, it said. The Election Commission said it reviewed the “current situation” regarding the scheduled elections in Poonch. It noted that according to a report it received from the AJK home secretary, there were “concerns over the law and order situation in some areas of Poonch district and Pallandri district”. “Moreover, the Election Commission received requests from some political personalities and candidates hailing from these districts, in which it has been requested to postpone the elections in Poonch district and Pallandri district considering the current situation,” the press release read. The electoral watchdog said it will announce the new polling dates and a revised election schedule for Poonch and Pallandri after reviewing the situation and “considering all relevant matters”. The commission clarified that the decision to postpone some of the polls was taken “only in the context of the current law and order situation to ensure that elections are held in a free, fair, transparent and peaceful environment”. The Election Commission’s decision comes in the wake of clashes that took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Poonch district’s Rawalakot on July 27, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. Rawalakot has been gripped by unrest since early June , with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) staging sit-ins periodically. The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now. The government has accused militant elements “pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest. Earlier this week, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal noted that the “law and order situation and the demands of the safety of voters play an important role in holding elections”. Responding to a question, he had said that under the AJK constitution, the current Legislative Assembly ceases to exist after August 4. “Even if elections cannot be held in two or a few more constituencies, one cannot say that the house is not complete or those who have returned cannot take oath or perform their functions,” he explained. He said the new assembly would still take oath after the completion of the August 10 polls.

items.title: Anambra First Lady, Nonye Soludo wins BudgIT 2026 Active Citizens Award
items.description: By Vincent Ujum adu AWKA – Wife of the Anambra State Governor, Dr. Nonye Soludo, has emerged winner of the health activism category at the 2026 BudgIT Active Citizens Awards. The award, in its third edition, recognises individuals and organisations making outstanding contributions to civic engagement, social development, accountability and sustainable development across Nigeria. Mrs Soludo was honoured for her efforts in advancing preventive healthcare, community wellness and public health advocacy through her non-governmental organisation, the Healthy Living with Nonye Soludo Initiative. She emerged winner ahead of Nigerian health and gender rights advocate, Ramatu Ada Ochekliye, and public health and social impact professional, Sidney Sampson, after a rigorous selection process that assessed nominees based on innovation, impact, sustainability, inclusion, leadership and measurable community outcomes. Receiving the award, Mrs Soludo described the recognition as a humbling honour and a renewed call to serve with greater commitment. She said the award belonged to members of the Healthy Living with Nonye Soludo Initiative, partners, healthcare workers, volunteers, community leaders and residents of Anambra State who had embraced the vision of wellness and healthy living. “Like a family driven by one common goal, we have shown that when communities take ownership of their health, lasting transformation becomes very possible,” she said. Mrs Soludo expressed appreciation to BudgIT, Civic Hive and the Ford Foundation for the recognition, adding that it would motivate the initiative to expand its reach and continue promoting healthier communities. In a statement, Senior Special Assistant to the wife of the governor, Mr. Daniel Ezeigwe, said the award reflected growing national recognition of the impact of Mrs Soludo’s healthy living campaign, which he described as a model for promoting preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyles. Ezeigwe said that since becoming Anambra First Lady, Dr. Soludo had championed several people-centred initiatives, including statewide fitness campaigns, maternal and child health advocacy, nutrition education, environmental sanitation, the Healthy Living Pad Bank for schoolgirls, free seed distribution to households and the Nonye’s Healthy Living Pap Initiative aimed at tackling childhood malnutrition. “These programmes have touched thousands of lives while reinforcing the importance of prevention as the foundation of a healthier society,” he said. He added that the recognition further highlighted Mrs Soludo’s commitment to improving the health and wellbeing of Anambra residents while contributing to Nigeria’s broader public health development. The post Anambra First Lady, Nonye Soludo wins BudgIT 2026 Active Citizens Award appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Luca Zidane sur le point de quitter Grenade pour Leganés
items.description: L’aventure de Luca Zidane , 28 ans, avec Grenade FC est sur le point de se terminer. Le gardien international s’apprête à quitter le club d’Andalousie pour rejoindre une équipe de la capitale espagnole Madrid, selon les informations du quotidien AS. Le transfert du fils du nouveau sélectionneur de l’équipe de France, la légende Zinedine Zidane, de Grenade vers Leganés (Seganda) est pratiquement scellé. Il ne reste que la signature qui pourrait intervenir ce vendredi 7 août, selon AS. Le gardien des Fennecs devrait quitter le FC Grenade où il est arrivé en 2024 après l’arrivée d’un nouveau gardien, Raúl Lizoain, 35 ans. La saison passée, il a disputé 27 matchs et encaissé 33 buts. Si son jeu de pied est apprécié en Espagne, il reste critiqué pour ses performances irrégulières, comme d’ailleurs chez les Verts. Luca Zidane, des performances irrégulières avec Grenade FC Durant la Coupe du 2026, il a encaissé six buts en trois matchs disputés contre l’Argentine (0-3) et la Jordanie (2-1) au premier tour, et la Suisse (0-2) en 16 es de finale. Des prestations qui lui ont valu des critiques acerbes en Algérie, et le sélectionneur Vladimir Petkovic a dû le remplacer face à l’Autriche (3-3) lors du dernier match de la phase de groupes. En revanche, Zidane a brillé lors des matchs amicaux contre l’Uruguay (0-0) et surtout face aux Pays-Bas (1-0) où il a sorti une performance XXL. En Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN 2025) au Maroc, il n’a encaissé que deux buts face au Nigéria en quarts de finale (0-2). L’article Luca Zidane sur le point de quitter Grenade pour Leganés est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Mental health crisis: Fewer than 300 psychiatrists serve over 200m Nigerians — Sheikh
items.description: … Demands urgent implementation of Mental Health Act, stronger funding By Chioma Obinna A Professor of Psychiatry at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, Prof. Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, has said that Nigeria is facing a deepening mental health crisis, with fewer than 300 psychiatrists available to serve a population of over 200 million people. Sheikh, a member of the Advisory Committee to Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Africa CDC, said the severe shortage of mental health professionals, inadequate funding and poor access to community-based services were widening the gap between Nigerians who need mental healthcare and those who receive it. He spoke at the Mental Health Leadership and Advocacy Public Lecture, where he called for urgent implementation of the Mental Health Act and stronger policy, financing and legislative reforms to strengthen Nigeria’s mental health system. According to him, mental health remains one of the most neglected areas of healthcare, particularly in Africa, despite its enormous impact on individuals, families, communities and national economies. “Legislation provides the skeleton, policy provides the direction, and financing provides the muscle. Closing the mental health systems gap requires all three to move together,” Sheikh said. He said Nigeria’s Mental Health Act, signed into law in December 2022, represented a major milestone but warned that the law would have limited impact without adequate funding, trained personnel, functional services and effective implementation. “Without legislation, policy is just paper. Without policy, legislation has no direction,” he stated. Sheikh said mental health services in Nigeria remained concentrated largely in federally owned tertiary psychiatric hospitals, most of which are located in state capitals and therefore out of reach of many people requiring care. He noted that although mental health had been recognised as a component of primary healthcare in Nigeria, mental health services remained largely unavailable at the primary healthcare level. The psychiatrist said the country’s shortage of specialists was compounded by inadequate numbers of psychologists, psychiatric nurses and other mental health professionals. He said trained psychiatric nurses were sometimes deployed to other duties because of the absence of functional mental health units and inadequate commitment to mental healthcare. Sheikh also expressed concern over poor financing, noting that mental health receives less than 3.5 per cent of the health budget, with more than 90 per cent of available mental health resources going to hospitals. He argued that such an arrangement was unsustainable and inconsistent with the goal of universal health coverage. “The treatment gap is about demand versus supply. Demand is all over, but barriers restrict access,” he said. To bridge the gap, Sheikh advocated a decentralised mental health system in which most people receive care at the lowest appropriate level, including self-care, community services and primary healthcare, while patients requiring specialised intervention are referred to higher levels of care. He called for greater integration of mental healthcare into primary healthcare and the adoption of task-shifting, whereby trained nurses, community health workers and other non-specialist health workers provide mental health services under appropriate supervision. “Treat at the lowest level. Integrate into primary healthcare. Task-shift. No discharge to nowhere,” he said. According to him, the “no discharge to nowhere” principle requires patients leaving psychiatric hospitals to be linked to community-based follow-up services rather than being discharged without continuing care. He said common conditions such as depression could be managed at the primary healthcare level through appropriate training and the World Health Organisation’s Mental Health Gap Action Programme, mhGAP. “Seventy per cent of mental health problems can be treated by trained doctors, nurses and primary health workers with adequate supervision and support,” Sheikh said. The professor warned that neglecting mental health could undermine Nigeria’s economic and social development, stressing that untreated mental health conditions impose significant costs on individuals, families, workplaces and governments. “Africa needs to invest in mental health as mental health is not only a key part of healthcare but also of education and labour. If ignored, the economic development of the countries in Africa will be compromised,” he said. “The message is clear for policymakers: invest in mental health and get good returns.” Sheikh also called for mental health to be integrated into education, employment, social protection and other sectors, arguing that mental healthcare cannot be addressed by the health sector alone. He urged stronger suicide prevention strategies, anti-stigma programmes and measures to protect the rights of people living with mental health conditions. The psychiatrist said Nigeria’s mental health legislation had historically been rooted in colonial-era laws focused largely on custodial care rather than treatment, recovery and human rights. He noted that mental health legislation in Nigeria dates back to 1916 and evolved into a law in 1959, retaining its colonial orientation for decades before the country eventually moved towards a modern rights-based framework. According to him, sustained advocacy by mental health professionals, civil society organisations, lawmakers, development partners and other stakeholders played a critical role in the eventual passage of the Mental Health Act. He, however, stressed that the passage of the law was only the beginning. “The Mental Health Act is a major achievement, but the real test is implementation,” he said. Sheikh called for sustainable domestic financing, stronger governance, reliable mental health data, adequate human resources, essential medicines and technologies, as well as effective monitoring of the implementation of the law and national mental health policy. He also advocated mental health parity in health insurance, anti-discrimination measures, school and workplace mental health programmes and greater protection of patients’ rights. The psychiatrist urged policymakers to involve people with lived experience of mental health conditions in the development of policies and legislation, saying their experiences were essential to building humane and effective services. He warned that stigma and discrimination continue to prevent many Nigerians from seeking help, often forcing people to present at hospitals only when their conditions have become severe. “Protecting the rights of persons with mental illness is not optional. Modern mental health legislation must be rights-based, promote autonomy and consent, provide the least restrictive care and ensure access to appropriate services,” he said. He called on the Federal Government and states to move mental healthcare closer to communities by integrating services into primary healthcare facilities and strengthening referral and follow-up systems. Sheikh also urged government to reduce dependence on donor funding by providing sustainable domestic resources for mental health. He said Nigeria could no longer afford to treat mental health as a peripheral issue, warning that the country’s development aspirations would remain threatened unless mental health was made a national priority. “Mental health is a significant part of development,” he said. Also speaking, Emeritus Professor of Psychiatry at the University of Ibadan and Director of the WHO Collaborating Centre, Ibadan, Prof. Oye Gureje, stressed the importance of strong leadership and sustained advocacy in tackling Nigeria’s mental healthcare challenges and driving reforms across Africa Gureje explained that the Mental Health Leadership and Advocacy Programme, now in its 13th edition, was established to develop leaders capable of influencing policy, mobilising stakeholders and championing improvements in mental health systems. He noted that there is growing global recognition that “there is no health without mental health,” stressing that mental disorders remain common, underdiagnosed and inadequately treated despite their impact on individuals, families and national productivity. According to him, inadequate funding, weak political commitment and poor implementation of policies have contributed significantly to the treatment gap. He said trained leaders and advocates were needed to keep mental health on the policy agenda, raise public awareness and pressure governments to prioritise quality mental healthcare. Speaking, the Head of the Division of Disease Control and Prevention at the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Africa CDC, Dr Mohammed Abdulaziz, also called for stronger leadership, reform of outdated mental health laws and adoption of a public health approach to close Africa’s widening mental healthcare gap. Abdulaziz said the Africa CDC Mental Health Leadership Programme was established to develop leaders capable of driving policy reforms and strengthening mental health systems across the continent. He said the programme rests on four pillars: the Kofi Annan Fellowship, the Field Epidemiology Training Programme, FETP, short leadership and advocacy courses, and support for civil society organisations and people with lived experience of mental health conditions. He disclosed that Africa CDC was supporting countries including The Gambia and Sierra Leone to modernise their mental health laws, while encouraging other countries to adopt rights-based legislation. Abdulaziz urged African governments to replace archaic laws that stigmatise people living with mental health conditions, strengthen surveillance and research, and generate evidence to guide policymaking. He called for a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to mental health. “We cannot continue to say mental health is underfunded without making deliberate efforts to change the narrative,” Abdulaziz said, reaffirming Africa CDC’s commitment to supporting mental health reforms across the continent. The post Mental health crisis: Fewer than 300 psychiatrists serve over 200m Nigerians — Sheikh appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Grand Magal de Touba : la Police nationale dresse son bilan sécuritaire avec 244 interpellations
items.description: La Police nationale sénégalaise a présenté le bilan de son dispositif de sécurisation déployé à l'occasion de la 132ème édition du Grand Magal de Touba. Un dispositif massif de 4 823 fonctionnaires, appuyé par des drones, caméras de vidéoprotection, système anti-drones et outils de détection, a été mobilisé pour encadrer les millions de pèlerins. Sur le plan répressif, 244 personnes ont été interpellées, dont 110 déférées au Parquet, renseigne le communiqué rendu public dans la soirée du 6 aout. La lutte contre les stupéfiants a permis la saisie de plusieurs kilos de chanvre indien, de comprimés d'ecstasy et de médicaments détournés comme le Tapentadol. Côté circulation, les contrôles routiers ont donné lieu à l'immobilisation de 70 véhicules (voitures et motos confondus) et à la perception de plus de 2,4 millions de francs CFA d'amendes. Mais le bilan reste endeuillé : 68 accidents ont été recensés, faisant 2 morts et 43 blessés. Volet humanitaire et social Le service médical de la police a assuré près de 490 consultations gratuites et distribué 2 000 bouteilles d'eau. Sur le plan social, 27 enfants égarés ont été pris en charge, dont 6 restaient non réclamés au moment du bilan. Par ailleurs, 200 passeports ont été délivrés en moins de 48 heures, facilitant les démarches administratives des pèlerins. La Police nationale a conclu son communiqué en adressant ses remerciements aux autorités religieuses et aux populations, tout en présentant ses condoléances aux familles des victimes d'accidents. O.B.N

items.title: More appalling APC arrogance! By Donu Kogbara
items.description: Last week, I complained about the arrogance displayed by Dave Umahi, the Minister of Works, who has a lot of questions to answer around the mysterious death in his compound of an attractive young female nurse. This week, I will focus on another example of APC arrogance. Following a visit to the presidential villa by the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN), His Eminence, Cardinal John Olorunfemi Onaiyekan, the emeritus archbishop of Abuja, gave an interview in which he described Tinubu’s nonchalant response when the bishops expressed concerns about the widespread suffering in the country. They told him that the country was bleeding. He disagreed and said the economy is doing fine. They said they were very worried about the hunger in the land. He said that hunger existed before he was born, displaying a reluctance to take responsibility for the hunger that has increased under his watch. An uproar ensued as opposition politicians, mainstream journalists, Christians generally, some Muslims, anti-APC social media influencers, professional humanitarians who run charities, etc, and members of the general public accused Mr President of chronic insensitivity Villa aparatchiks, alarmed by how bad the above remarks made their boss look, flew to his defence and accused Onaiyekan of breaching confidentiality by repeating the contents of a private interaction. Meanwhile, pro-APC social media influencers insulted Onaiyekan. Some even depicted him wearing demonic horns. The National Executive Council of the Catholic Laity Council of Nigeria (CLCN) addressed these complaints in a letter thus: It is the Catholic church’s God-given duty to speak truth to power, defend the vulnerable and hold leadership accountable “with truth and charity”. The bishops, priests and laity are called to be “salt of the earth and light of the world” (Matthew 5:13-14), even in the corridors of power. While the church respects the sanctity of private engagements, “matters that touch on the life, welfare and future of over 200 million Nigerians cannot remain forever in closed rooms.” “Cardinal Onaiyekan did not reveal secrets. He shared the moral concerns of the church and response of government, which is in the public interest.” Onaiyekan spoke out of concern, not malice because he is a man of peace and integrity who believes in dialogue. Government and church should continue to work together for the common good. We should pray for our leaders and support policies that bring relief to the poor, security to our communities and justice to all. Now, fair-minded people like me know that Tinubu cannot be blamed for every systemic dysfunction in a country that has been on the wrong path for decades. But, as one of his many detractors has eloquently pointed out (in an anonymous online article), “leadership is judged by results rather than historical context”. And there is no getting away from the fact that Tinubu is the personification of arrogance, delusion and gaslighting. I’m convinced that there is no humble, intellectually honest or genuinely compassionate bone in that man’s body!!! And his response to the bishops proves his penchant for hubris and callousness. Meanwhile, there are 38 million Catholics in Nigeria, including me and a whole bunch of very senior APC stalwarts – the Senate President (Godswill Akpabio), the Chairman of the APC Governors Forum (Hope Uzodinma) and others too numerous to mention in this short column. One of the above, George Akume, the Secretary to Government, has decided to stick his neck out and play peacemaker and placate both his religious and political constituencies. According to Akume, the Tinubu administration remains fully open to deepening its relationship with and receiving sincere counsel from religious institutions…and regards constructive engagement with the CBCN and other faith-based organizations as essential to navigating Nigeria’s economic and security challenges. I salute Akume for trying, but it is too late. Tinubu has already soured the milk. I also, of course, salute Onaiyekan. He has done better than the likes of Adeboye who are always making excuses for Tinubu, probably for reasons linked to ethnic loyalty. And, by the way, I thank God that Onaiyekan is a Yoruba from Kogi State because he cannot be accused of criticizing Tinubu for anti-Yoruba reasons. Better still, because he is not from the southeast, he cannot be viciously attacked the way the Yoruba wing of the APC constantly attacks Igbos, either subtly or overtly and especially online. Also, when a man who is notoriously suspicious of other tribes needs to be cautioned, his own brother is more likely than an outsider to persuade him to change direction. And I guess it’s possible that Tinubu will eventually listen to Onaiyekan’s advice. Finally, let’s hope that the many Catholics who are slavishly follow-following Tinubu have heard our spiritual leaders clearly stating that his government’s performance is morally indefensible. Frankly, they should hide their heads in shame. DONU’S WORLD I have a YouTube channel. It’s called DONU’S WORLD. https://youtube.com/@donukogbara?si=bBm_IPdFZ_wUyKYq NIGERIA UNFILTERED – spicy commentaries on Naija issues – appears every Wednesday, while DONU’S WEEK appears on Fridays and is international as well as local and covers a mish-mash of soft and tough issues around my personal life, my work and my worldview. Two days ago, in this week’s Nigeria Unfiltered video, I focussed on Peter Obi’s belief that Southeast governors who have defected to APC cannot drag their people along. I said I hoped he wasn’t being too optimistic, given how easy it can be to manipulate the Nigerian masses. Please check out my Donu’s World library (dating back to early 2024) on YouTube, plus the new videos I produce every week. items.title: Health Minister seeks Catholic Church’s support to complete stalled Agenda 111 hospitals
items.description: The Minister for Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has appealed to faith-based organisations, particularly the Catholic Church, to partner with the government in completing some of the stalled Agenda 111 hospital projects across the country. According to the Ministry of Health, the Minister made the appeal during an engagement with Bishops of the Catholic Church, where he outlined government’s efforts to address challenges affecting the implementation of the Agenda 111 programme. Mr Akandoh acknowledged that several of the hospital projects have stalled due to funding constraints, leaving many of the facilities incomplete and yet to serve the communities they were intended to benefit. He explained that the government is currently prioritising the completion of 35 of the projects to ensure they become fully operational and begin delivering essential healthcare services. The Minister said the government was open to partnerships with faith-based organisations, including the Catholic Church, to manage some of the completed hospitals on a non-profit basis. Under the proposed arrangement, the government would provide the required health professionals and technical support, while faith-based institutions would contribute their expertise in healthcare management and service delivery. Mr Akandoh stressed that faith-based organisations have long played a vital role in Ghana’s health sector and said strengthening collaboration with them would help improve access to quality healthcare and enhance the country’s health infrastructure. Responding to the proposal, the President of the Ghana Catholic Bishops’ Conference, Most Rev. Matthew Kwasi Gyamfi, welcomed the initiative and commended the Minister’s efforts to deepen cooperation between the Ministry of Health and faith-based health institutions. He also called for stronger collaboration to ensure that the existing capacity within religious health facilities is fully harnessed to support Ghana’s national healthcare objectives.

items.title: Coastal Highway: We have moved beyond Epe, Umahi replies Duke
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA – Minister of Works, Engr. Dave Umahi, has said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway project has moved beyond Epe in Lagos State and is currently ongoing across five states. Umahi stated this in response to concerns raised by former Cross River State Governor, Donald Duke, that the project might not progress beyond Epe. The minister spoke during an inspection of Section 4B of the highway in Ondo State, according to a statement issued on Friday by his Senior Special Assistant on Media, Francis Nwaze. He said, “The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is already on. We have sailed past Lagos that my brother Donald Duke talked about. “We are on in Ogun — 28 kilometres of dual carriageway. We are on in Ondo — 52 kilometres of dual carriageway. We are also on in Calabar — 27 kilometres. In Akwa Ibom, the first section is about 47 kilometres. Those ones are over 60 per cent done.” Umahi added that construction had also commenced on the longest stretch of the project, a 180-kilometre dual carriageway section in Akwa Ibom State. The minister described the coastal highway as one of the flagship infrastructure projects of President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, saying it would not only connect states but also create employment opportunities and boost economic activities along the corridor. “Roads mean employment. In this section alone, Hitech has employed over 1,000 people. Direct and indirect jobs are springing up. “Anywhere we are working, you will see security presence. We also have local vigilantes working with them. It is opening up commerce, agriculture and education,” he said. Umahi urged residents of the Niger Delta region to support the project, insisting that those criticising the highway were not acting in the interest of the people. “It is up to Niger Delta people to speak up for this project. They should defend it. They should defend the President. They must vote for the President to complete it,” he said. On allegations that the highway alignment was altered to favour private estates, the minister explained that the original coastal route was abandoned due to technical challenges, including deep soil deposits of up to 50 metres and the need to construct three bridges of about 3.5 kilometres each across ocean channels. “That option was not feasible. It would have been too expensive,” he said. Addressing concerns over funding, Umahi described the project as one of the most transparent infrastructure initiatives undertaken by the Federal Government. He said Deutsche Bank, which is financing Section 1 of the highway, had described the design and construction as being “in perfection” and had oversubscribed the loan facility by $100 million. The minister commended Hitech Construction Company for the quality of work and its engagement with host communities, expressing confidence that the project would be completed as promised by President Tinubu. “Under President Tinubu, this country will be rebuilt. The roads he is building now will last for the next 100 years without reconstruction,” Umahi said. He urged Nigerians to continue to offer constructive criticism, stressing that the administration remained open to feedback aimed at improving governance. items.title: Royaume-Uni-Maroc : les échanges changent progressivement d'échelle
items.description: Les échanges commerciaux entre le Royaume-Uni et le Maroc ont atteint un niveau inédit sur les douze mois achevés à fin mars 2026, à 5,3 milliards de livres sterling. Tirée par une envolée des exportations britanniques, cette dynamique réduit fortement le déficit commercial de Londres et confirme le renforcement progressif des relations économiques entre les deux pays. Les relations économiques entre le Royaume-Uni et le Maroc changent progressivement d'échelle. Portés par une forte accélération des exportations britanniques, les échanges bilatéraux ont atteint un niveau inédit sur douze mois glissants à fin mars 2026. Si le Royaume-Uni demeure un partenaire commercial de second rang dans le commerce extérieur marocain, la dynamique observée confirme un approfondissement des relations économiques entre les deux pays, dans un contexte où Londres cherche à consolider sa présence sur les marchés à forte croissance. En l'espace d'un an, le commerce bilatéral a progressé de 16,7% pour atteindre 5,3 milliards de livres sterling sur les quatre trimestres achevés à fin mars 2026, soit l'équivalent d'environ 6,3 milliards d'euros. Il s'agit d'un gain de 756 millions de livres par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente. La progression est principalement alimentée par les ventes britanniques vers le Maroc. Les exportations du Royaume-Uni ont bondi de 29,8% sur un an pour atteindre 2,6 milliards de livres, tandis que les importations britanniques en provenance du Maroc n'ont progressé que de 6,3%, à 2,7 milliards de livres. Un déséquilibre commercial qui se réduit nettement L'un des enseignements les plus significatifs du rapport concerne l'évolution du solde commercial. Le déficit commercial du Royaume-Uni vis-à-vis du Maroc s'est fortement réduit, passant de 546 millions de livres à seulement 112 millions de livres sur un an. Cette amélioration résulte essentiellement de la montée en puissance des exportations britanniques de biens, qui permettent désormais au Royaume-Uni de dégager un excédent commercial sur les échanges de marchandises de 160 millions de livres, alors qu'il affichait encore un déficit de 205 millions un an auparavant. Le déficit britannique subsiste toutefois dans les échanges de services, où les importations en provenance du Maroc restent supérieures aux exportations britanniques. L'énergie propulse les exportations britanniques La structure des échanges met en évidence le poids croissant des produits énergétiques. Le pétrole brut devient, de loin, la première exportation britannique vers le Maroc, avec 630,6 millions de livres, représentant près d'un tiers des exportations de marchandises. Les minerais métalliques arrivent en deuxième position avec 315,7 millions de livres (+48,1%), devant les générateurs mécaniques (219,4 millions), les produits pétroliers raffinés (197,3 millions) et les automobiles (112,5 millions). Dans le sens inverse, les exportations marocaines vers le Royaume-Uni demeurent largement dominées par les produits agricoles. Les fruits et légumes représentent 644,4 millions de livres, soit plus du tiers des importations britanniques en provenance du Maroc. Viennent ensuite les équipements électriques intermédiaires (386,9 millions), les voitures (153,2 millions), les meubles (141,8 millions) et les vêtements (112,8 millions). Cette composition illustre une complémentarité croissante entre les deux économies : d'un côté, des exportations britanniques à forte composante industrielle et énergétique ; de l'autre, une offre marocaine concentrée sur l'agroalimentaire, l'industrie manufacturière et certaines filières automobiles. Les services gagnent également du terrain Les services représentent désormais près de 29% des échanges bilatéraux. Les exportations britanniques de services vers le Maroc ont progressé de 15,1% pour atteindre 625 millions de livres. Les services de transport constituent le premier poste (258 millions de livres), devant les voyages (130 millions) et les services aux entreprises (103 millions). À l'inverse, les importations britanniques de services marocains demeurent très largement concentrées sur les dépenses liées aux voyages, qui représentent près de 80% du total, avec 717 millions de livres. Une relation économique qui monte en puissance Au-delà des seuls flux commerciaux, plusieurs indicateurs témoignent d'un renforcement progressif de la place du Royaume-Uni dans l'économie marocaine. En 2024, la part de marché britannique dans les importations marocaines de biens et de services est passée à 2,8%, contre 2,5% un an auparavant. La progression est particulièrement visible dans les biens, où cette part atteint 2,5%. Le tissu économique britannique impliqué dans les échanges avec le Maroc continue également de s'élargir. En 2025, environ 2.100 entreprises britanniques exportaient des marchandises vers le Maroc, tandis que près de 900 importaient des produits marocains. Le rapport souligne également l'importance croissante des chaînes de valeur. Selon les estimations de l'OCDE, les exportations vers le Royaume-Uni soutenaient environ 286.300 emplois au Maroc en 2022, contre un peu plus de 10.000 emplois britanniques liés aux exportations vers le Maroc. Enfin, les projections du FMI reprises dans le document tablent sur une croissance de l'économie marocaine de 4,9% en 2026, avant un léger ralentissement à 4,5% en 2027. Dans le même temps, le PIB nominal devrait franchir le seuil des 194 milliards de dollars dès cette année, confortant l'attractivité du pays auprès des investisseurs et de ses partenaires commerciaux. The post Royaume-Uni-Maroc : les échanges changent progressivement d'échelle appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Four injured as tanker fire hits Abuja filling station
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Four persons sustained injuries on Thursday night after a petroleum tanker caught fire while discharging products at AYM Shafa Filling Station, beside the Federal Capital Territory Internal Revenue Service (FCT-IRS) office along Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti Way, Area 3, Garki, Abuja. The Federal Fire Service (FFS) confirmed that the incident involved a tanker carrying about 60,000 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS). In a statement issued on Friday, the National Public Relations Officer and Head of Corporate Services, FFS Headquarters, DCF Paul Abraham, said the fire had been successfully extinguished following a coordinated emergency response operation. He said the inferno affected part of the adjoining three-storey FCT-IRS building before firefighters contained it using multiple firefighting appliances, medium water jets and foam compound. The Controller-General of the Federal Fire Service, Olumode Samuel Adeyemi, who acted as Incident Commander, personally coordinated the operation and remained at the scene until the early hours of Friday to ensure the fire was completely brought under control. According to the statement, the four injured adult males were evacuated by a National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) ambulance to a nearby hospital, where they received treatment and were later discharged. The FFS said a thorough inspection of the scene confirmed that there was no further fire outbreak or casualty, adding that all responding personnel and equipment had returned safely to their stations. The Service commended residents, motorists and members of the public for their patience, cooperation and compliance with safety directives during the emergency response. It also acknowledged the support of sister agencies, including the FCT Fire Service, NEMA, the Nigeria Police Force and other emergency responders, for their roles in managing the incident. The FFS added that investigation had commenced to determine the immediate and remote causes of the fire, with a view to preventing future occurrences. “The Federal Fire Service remains committed to safeguarding lives, property and critical national assets through prompt, professional and coordinated emergency response,” the statement added. The post Four injured as tanker fire hits Abuja filling station appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La CAF vole au secours d’Infantino et de la FIFA
items.description: Le Comité exécutif de la Confédération Africaine de Football (CAF) a approuvé à l'unanimité, jeudi, la « Mise à jour conjointe » publiée par le président de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, et le secrétaire général, Mattias Grafström, au sujet du projet controversé FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). Dans le document dont la CAF a pris note, la présidence de la FIFA reconnaît que « des erreurs ont été commises dans le cadre du processus relatif à la proposition » et assure qu'il n'était pas dans son intention d'écarter le Conseil de la FIFA et ses associations membres de la démarche. La FIFA présente ses excuses pour ces erreurs et s'engage à ce qu'elles ne se reproduisent pas. Concrètement, la proposition — qui devait être soumise au vote des associations membres et du Conseil — est retirée, et un rapport d'examen sera présenté lors de la prochaine réunion du Conseil de la FIFA. La direction de la fédération mondiale tient toutefois à préciser que tout ce qui a été fait est resté en pleine conformité avec le cadre réglementaire de la FIFA, malgré les erreurs commises. Motsepe insiste sur la gouvernance et la transparence Réagissant à cette mise à jour, le président de la CAF, Patrice Motsepe, a salué la démarche de la FIFA et réaffirmé l'attachement de son organisation aux standards internationaux. « La CAF accueille favorablement et approuve la “Mise à jour conjointe” du Président de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, et du Secrétaire Général, Mattias Grafström. La CAF continuera de se concentrer sur son objectif de faire du football africain l’un des meilleurs au monde et réaffirme son engagement à respecter les meilleures pratiques internationales en matière de gouvernance, de transparence et d’audit. Pour nous, en Afrique, le respect de la gouvernance, des procédures régulières et de la transparence est essentiel et non négociable, car il s’agit de la pratique et de la conduite que nous attendons de nos gouvernements, entreprises, institutions et organisations », assure le président de la CAF. Patrice Motsepe de poursuivre. « C’est également la conduite attendue de la CAF. Nous sommes déterminés à continuer de travailler avec la FIFA, ses Associations Membres, les autres Confédérations de football et les parties prenantes afin de préserver et de respecter les meilleures pratiques internationales en matière de gouvernance, de procédures régulières et de transparence, et de contribuer au développement et à la croissance du football dans le monde. La CAF continuera également de se concentrer sur le développement de nos jeunes footballeurs et footballeuses, entraîneurs et formateurs, des Équipes Nationales de nos 54 Associations Membres, ainsi que des ligues amateurs et professionnelles sur le continent africain. Des progrès encourageants sont réalisés dans les discussions avec nos sponsors, partenaires et investisseurs actuels et nouveaux afin de garantir que la CAF continue d’être financièrement autonome et indépendante, et que les stades ainsi que les autres infrastructures de football soient construits et modernisés. Des progrès sont également réalisés dans les préparatifs de la TotalEnergies CAF Coupe d’Afrique des Nations (“CAN”) Kenya Tanzanie Ouganda (“PAMOJA”) et des autres compétitions de la CAF. » Soutien réaffirmé à Infantino Au-delà de l'épisode FFE, le Comité exécutif a tenu à renouveler son soutien à Gianni Infantino, remercié pour son appui constant au football africain, de même que Mattias Grafström et l'administration de la FIFA, salués pour l'organisation de la Coupe du Monde 2026. items.title: Wontumi applies for bail pending appeal after imprisonment at Nsawam Prison
items.description: The Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Wontumi, has filed an application at the High Court seeking bail pending the determination of his appeal against his conviction. The application, filed on August 5, 2026, states that the first appellant is currently incarcerated at the Nsawam Medium Security Prisons. The Notice of Motion, filed by his lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea of Zoe, Akyea & Co., invokes Section 96(1) of the Criminal and Other Offences (Procedure) Act, 1960 (Act 30) and Section 33(1) of the Courts Act, 1993 (Act 459). The application prays the court to admit Wontumi to bail pending the hearing and determination of his appeal, relying on the grounds set out in an accompanying affidavit. The case is titled The Republic v. Bernard Antwi Boasiako @ Wontumi, Kwame Antwi (at large), and Akonta Mining Company Limited, with Wontumi listed as the first appellant/applicant and Akonta Mining Company Limited as the third appellant. The application has been scheduled to be moved before the High Court, Criminal Division ‘4’ in Accra on August 19, 2026. Copies of the application have been served on the Office of the Attorney-General as the respondent, as well as the Director of the Nsawam Medium Security Prisons. The High Court is expected to determine whether Wontumi should be granted bail while his appeal against the conviction is pending. Chairman Wontumi was sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment after Criminal Court 4 Division of the High Court found him guilty on all six charges brought against him. He, together with Akonta Mining Limited and a third accused person, Kwame Antwi, was prosecuted over illegal mining activities on the company’s concession at Samreboi in the Western Region. Prosecutors said the accused unlawfully assigned mineral rights on the concession without the approval of the sector minister and facilitated mining operations without the required authorisation, contrary to the Minerals and Mining Act.

items.title: 66ᵉ anniversaire de la Côte d’Ivoire : « Nous nous inspirerons du modèle ivoirien… », dit Bah Oury reçu à la Primature
items.description: En visite en Côte d’Ivoire pour représenter le président guinéen, Mamadi Doumbouya, aux festivités marquant le 66ᵉ anniversaire de l’Indépendance du pays, le Premier ministre Amadou Oury Bah a été reçu en audience ce jeudi par son homologue ivoirien, Dr Beugré Mambé. Les deux chefs de gouvernement ont échangé sur les relations entre la Guinée et la Côte d’Ivoire, ainsi que sur les perspectives de coopération entre les deux pays. À l’issue de la rencontre, Amadou Oury Bah a salué les performances économiques et les avancées de la Côte d’Ivoire, qu’il présente comme une source d’inspiration pour la Guinée. « La Côte d’Ivoire est une référence dans la région. Nous nous inspirons du modèle ivoirien pour être plus performants et nous développer dans différents domaines », a déclaré le Premier ministre guinéen, cité par la Primature ivoirienne. De son côté, Dr Beugré Mambé, s’exprimant au nom du président Alassane Ouattara, a souhaité la bienvenue à la délégation guinéenne. Il a également souligné les liens historiques et humains qui unissent les deux pays. « La coopération entre la Guinée et la Côte d’Ivoire est naturelle parce que les deux pays sont liés par un même destin », a rappelé le chef du gouvernement ivoirien. Cette année, l’Indépendance ivoirienne est célébrée ce vendredi 7 août dans la commune de Yopougon, choisie pour accueillir les festivités. Dans son adresse à la nation, le président Alassane Ouattara a présenté Yopougon comme « une commune qui incarne l’énergie de notre jeunesse, la diversité de notre peuple, le dynamisme et la vitalité de la Côte d’Ivoire moderne ». Mediaguinee L’article 66ᵉ anniversaire de la Côte d’Ivoire : « Nous nous inspirerons du modèle ivoirien… », dit Bah Oury reçu à la Primature est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Le FC Barcelone annule son match amical prévu à Tanger
items.description: Le FC Barcelone ne se rendra finalement pas au Maroc cet été. Le club catalan a annoncé, jeudi soir, l'annulation du match amical qu'il devait disputer le 15 août à Tanger face à une équipe marocaine dont l'identité n'avait pas encore été révélée. Dans un communiqué, le Barça explique avoir pris cette décision en raison d'un contexte jugé incertain. « Compte tenu du contexte d'incertitude actuel, le FC Barcelone estime que les conditions ne sont pas réunies pour la tenue de ce match », a indiqué le club, sans fournir davantage de précisions sur les raisons de cette annulation. Cette décision intervient un peu plus d'une semaine après l'annonce officielle du déplacement. Le 29 juillet, le conseil d'administration du FC Barcelone avait confirmé qu'il finalisait l'organisation de cette rencontre amicale à Tanger, dans le cadre de la préparation de l'équipe première pour la saison 2026-2027. Le club marocain qui devait affronter les Blaugrana n'avait jamais été officiellement dévoilé. L'annulation de cette affiche prive ainsi les supporters marocains d'un rendez-vous très attendu avec le champion d'Espagne, qui devait retrouver le Royaume dans le cadre de sa préparation estivale. items.title: 3 suspects including foreign national picked up by police over suspected cocaine seized in Tema
items.description: A Dutch national and two other suspects have been picked by the police as key suspects in the 866 parcels of a white powdered substance suspected to be cocaine. The substance, which according to the police has a street value of around US$6.9 million were concealed in sacks of gari at the Tema Port enclave. It was an intelligence-led operation that led to the arrest by the Tema police. The police have named the suspects Gilano Horwin, aged 31. The others are John Mensah Sabah, 41; and Alhaji Iddris Haruna. The police intercepted the 40-foot container, which was being loaded with the parcels. The Tema Regional Police Commander, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCOP) Eric Asamoah Asiedu, at a press briefing on Thursday (August 6, 2026), a separate narcotics operation on the same day als resulted in the arrest of another suspect. DCOP Asamoah Asiedu said the Command received intelligence at about 7:15 p.m. on August 5, 2026, that some young men were loading parcels of a white substance concealed in sacks of gari into a 40-foot container at a warehouse within the Tema Port enclave. He said the consignment was being prepared for export when a police team arrived at the scene and found three men who supervising the loading operation. According to DCOP Asamoah Asiedu, the container was mounted on a white DAF truck with registration number WR 1118-10. The suspects, together with the truck, were taken to the Tema Regional Police headquarters. He said a search of the sacks led to the recovery of 866 parcels of a white substance suspected to be cocaine, with an estimated value of US$6,928,000. DCOP Asamoah Asiedu said during interrogation, Owin allegedly stated that the substance was cocaine and claimed ownership of it. The three suspects have been detained to assist investigations, while the exhibits have been secured for forensic examination to determine the exact nature of the substance. The Regional Commander said investigations were ongoing. In a separate operation on the same day, the Prampram District Police intercepted a taxi allegedly transporting substances suspected to be Indian hemp. DCOP Asamoah Asiedu said the Tsopoli Police received information at about 5 p.m. on August 5, 2026, that the taxi was being pursued.

items.title: Revue de presse de ce vendredi 7 août 2026
items.description: Voici les principaux titres développés par la presse nationale de ce vendredi 7 août 2026 L’Economiste PLF 2027: Nouveau cycle budgétaire Le gouvernement prépare une nouvelle phase d’arbitrages budgétaires où il s’agira de serrer les dépenses sans freiner l’investissement. Les réunions consacrées à ces arbitrages débuteront en septembre, avec des propositions qui devront s’appuyer sur les capacités réelles de réalisation des projets et sur une programmation plus rigoureuse des dépenses publiques. Le Matin Frais du temps aménagé : dernière planche de salut pour l’université publique, ou premier pas vers sa privatisation ? À moins d’un mois de la rentrée universitaire 2026-2027, le débat sur les frais du temps aménagé n’a jamais été aussi vif. Pour la première fois, une grille tarifaire harmonisée impose à l’ensemble des fonctionnaires et salariés inscrits dans ce dispositif de payer leur formation, sur la base de la loi 59-24, jusqu’à 20.000 dirhams par an pour un doctorat. «Le Matin» a recueilli, auprès d’une source gouvernementale proche du dossier, les arguments qui sous-tendent la réforme, avant de les confronter à une contestation qui, des tribunaux administratifs à l’Institution du Médiateur du Royaume, ne faiblit pas. Les Inspirations Eco Le déficit change de caisse La loi 54.23 confie à la CNSS la gestion de l’assurance maladie obligatoire du secteur public, exercée jusqu’ici par la CNOPS. Prévu pour février 2027, le transfert porte sur un régime déficitaire depuis 2021, dont les réserves devraient s’épuiser sous peu. Ni le plafond de cotisation, figé depuis 2005, ni le tarif de remboursement, arrêté en 2006, ne sont revus avant le transfert. Libération Les vrais rouages d’une cabale anti-marocaine La mise en cause du Maroc dans l’organisation du Mondial 2030 à la suite des « vagues migratoires » vers Sebta illustre un mécanisme de manipulation politique et de propagande médiatique ciblée. Début août 2026, des formations politiques de gauche en Europe (notamment la coalition Sumar en Espagne et le parti Livre au Portugal) ont déposé des propositions parlementaires réclamant l’exclusion du Maroc ou le réexamen de la co-organisation du Mondial 2030. Al Bayane MRE : Des paroles aux actes Le siège national du Parti du progrès et du socialisme abritera, ce vendredi 07 août 2026 à 17 heures, une « Conférence spéciale », intitulée : « MRE : Des paroles aux actes ». Cet événement est organisé par le PPS en partenariat avec Cap Sud MRE et Good VIBES, deux structures d’accompagnement des Marocains du monde. L’objectif de cette initiative est de dépasser les discours démagogiques pour proposer des solutions réalistes et équitables à l’égard des Marocains Du Monde (MDM), sur les plans politique, juridique, économique et administratif. Al Massae Fédération de chasse : dossiers graves et appels à l’ouverture d’une enquête urgente La Fédération Royale Marocaine de Chasse vit au rythme d’événements étranges, dont certains frôlent l’absurde, particulièrement dans la région de Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceïma, alors que la Fédération garde un silence absolu sur ce qui se passe. Il y a quelques jours, lors d’une assemblée générale qui suscite de nombreuses interrogations, Rachid Chbihi a été reconduit à la tête de la section régionale de la fédération de chasse, au moment même où celle-ci s’enfonce dans un marasme de dossiers graves, ayant récemment atterri devant la justice. Assabah « La trésorerie » de l’Intérieur récupère des milliards détournés La caisse du ministère de l’Intérieur poursuit ses opérations de récupération des fonds publics indûment utilisés par certaines collectivités. À Casablanca, la commune a restitué plus de 650 millions de centimes en espèces, un montant largement supérieur au plafond légal fixé à 20 000 dirhams. Cette restitution illustre l’ampleur des irrégularités détectées et la volonté des autorités de resserrer le contrôle sur la gestion financière locale, dans un contexte où plusieurs dossiers similaires sont en cours d’examen.
